name: Working Capital Timing
title: Working Capital Timing
answer: Working capital timing covers the deliberate scheduling of cash inflows from receivables and outflows to payables to shorten the cash conversion cycle. In an AI accounting context, this means using models to predict when customers will pay, when suppliers should be paid, and how early payment discounts or late payment penalties affect liquidity. The page addresses both operational finance teams and controllers who need to balance supplier relationships against days sales outstanding and days payable outstanding.

sections.body: Working capital timing covers the deliberate scheduling of cash inflows from receivables and outflows to payables to shorten the cash conversion cycle. In an AI accounting context, this means using models to predict when customers will pay, when suppliers should be paid, and how early payment discounts or late payment penalties affect liquidity. The page addresses both operational finance teams and controllers who need to balance supplier relationships against days sales outstanding and days payable outstanding.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on data drawn from enterprise resource planning systems, bank transaction feeds, invoicing platforms, and customer or supplier master files. These sources are typically connected through application programming interfaces or scheduled file transfers into a data warehouse or lakehouse. Processing often happens on cloud infrastructure with standard database and workflow tools, not specialized hardware. The models need clean, timestamped records of invoice dates, due dates, payment dates, and credit terms.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners first build a historical dataset of payment behavior and invoice terms, then train supervised models to forecast payment dates and the probability of late payment. Optimization routines then suggest which invoices to pay early, which to hold, and which receivables to chase, subject to cash balance constraints and discount rules. The output is usually a daily or weekly recommended action list for treasury or accounts payable staff, with explanations for each recommendation. Human review remains common before any payment is released.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are data provenance, model drift, and the possibility of automated decisions that damage supplier or customer relationships. Access to bank and invoice data must be limited by role, and every model recommendation should be traceable to the underlying invoice and payment history. Compliance with accounting standards and internal controls requires that AI suggestions do not override segregation of duties or approval limits. Auditors may ask for evidence that the model was tested for bias against certain customer segments or payment terms.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Working capital timing tools are moving toward continuous, real-time cash forecasting that updates as invoices and payments arrive. Future systems may negotiate payment terms or send collection reminders automatically within policy boundaries, with humans handling exceptions. The likely direction is tighter integration between payables, receivables, and treasury, so that a single model optimizes the whole cash conversion cycle rather than separate silos.
